title: Tiered Dedicated Capacity Pricing & SLA Experiments (reserved GPUs, burst, autoscale)
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Run a set of pricing and packaging experiments for Dedicated Capacity to find a productized offering that balances conversion and unit economics for enterprise customers. Primary levers: reserved GPU commitments, burst credits/packs, autoscaling policies (pay-as-you-burst), and explicit SLA tiers (latency SLOs, uptime guarantees, support response). Deliverables: PRD listing price points, SLA definitions, contract addendum language, finance model, sales playbook, and an A/B experiment plan for pilot customers.
background: Sales and Solutions teams report friction converting trials to reserved commitments: customers want predictable capacity and SLAs but hesitate at all-in reserved pricing. Existing per-GPU and ad-hoc burst approaches create operational complexity and unpredictable revenue. We need a scalable packaging strategy that: 1) increases reserved commit conversion, 2) preserves margin versus hosted API, 3) allows safe burst/autoscale so customers don't overcommit.
proposal_options: Option A: Simple reserved SKU (per-GPU/month) + fixed burst credits. Lower complexity for sales but limited price discrimination.
Option B: Tiered SLA product (Standard/Business/Enterprise) that bundles reserved capacity ranges, different latency SLOs, and graduated support SLAs; burst sold as add-on packs or metered credits.
Option C: Usage-weighted hybrid — base reserved pool with additional metered autoscale at a premium rate; no formal SLA for smallest tiers; SLA applies to committed baseline only.
Option D: Commit discount ladder (volume/term), with optional autoscale buffer for short bursts billed at a higher effective rate; explicit penalty/credit model for SLA misses.
chosen_option: Hybrid: tiered SLA subscription (Standard/Business/Enterprise) with committed reserved pools, optional burst packs, and a metered autoscale rate. This balances conversion and predictability while allowing incremental revenue from bursts. Will A/B test the hybrid tier vs. legacy per-GPU pricing for pilot customers.
pricing_models_test_matrix: Experiment 1 (Pilot A): Hybrid Tiered vs. Legacy per-GPU — measure commit conversion rate, ARPU, churn over 90 days.
Experiment 2 (Pilot B): Add-on burst packs vs. metered autoscale — measure uptake, revenue delta, and support incidents during bursts.
Experiment 3 (Pilot C): Term discounts (12/24 months) impact on NRR and CAC payback period.
Primary metrics: conversion rate (trial->commit), ARPU, gross margin per GPU-hour, time-to-first-revenue, churn after 6 months, support/ops cost during bursts.
sla_tiers: Standard: up to 100 reserved GPU-hours/day. Latency SLO: p95 <= 600ms. Uptime target: 99.5%. Business-hours support (next-business-day).
Business: up to 1,000 reserved GPU-hours/day. Latency SLO: p95 <= 300ms. Uptime target: 99.9%. 24/5 support with 4-hour response SLA.

Enterprise: custom capacity. Latency SLO: p95 <= 100-200ms (profile-dependent). Uptime target: 99.95%+. 24/7 support with 1-hour response, runbooks, incident bridge, and optional dedicated capacity pools.
contract_questions_responses: Data isolation: Dedicated customers get isolated tenant pools and network segmentation; Private deployments offer VPC/on-prem for regulated workloads.
KMS and key management: Support customer-managed keys via AWS KMS/HSM integrations; legal requested CIAM language for key rotation responsibilities.
Audit & logging: SLA tiers include retention windows for audit logs; Enterprise tier includes extended retention and export tooling.
Breach notification and indemnity: Legal wants a capped liability clause for service outages; security will prepare a questionnaire response pack that maps to SOC2/ISO artifacts.
acceptance_criteria: Finalized PRD with clear price points and SLA definitions signed off by Finance, Sales, Legal, and Security.
Finance model shows target unit economics (>= 25% gross margin on committed usage after cost allocation) or a path to reach within 3 months of rollout.
Contract addendum drafted for new SLA tiers and burst billing terms, reviewed by Legal.
Sales playbook and enablement assets completed, including objection handling, calculators, and pricing tooling in CRM.
Pilot experiments instrumented in Console with dashboards (conversion, ARPU, margin) and clear gating for wider rollout.
Security questionnaire addendum completed and reviewed with two pilot customers.
